## PLAN ROUND 1 · publish · task first-edition

**Facts found**
- Three of the five runbooks name an internal host or a secret path:
  - runbooks/disk-full.md:3 names `db-primary-01.int.example.net`
  - runbooks/cert-expiry.md:3 names `secret/platform/acme-token`
  - runbooks/queue-backlog.md:3 names `jobs-01.int.example.net`
  - deploy-rollback.md and dns-failure.md name neither (search of runbooks/).
- The check enforces two rules:
  - every runbook opens with "Use when"
  - every relative link written `](./...)` resolves; links without `./` aren't checked
  
  (scripts/check.sh)
- A denylist grep for `.int.example.net` and `secret/` would catch all three lines. It would miss
  hosts on other domains and secret paths under other roots (scripts/check.sh).
- STANDARDS.md has one rule: "A runbook's first line says when to use it." (STANDARDS.md).
- The repository has no remote, no CI and no mkdocs.yml (.git/config, file search).
- No index of the runbooks exists (runbooks/, context/README.md).
- Every format sits behind single sign-on, and one access group grants all three. The audience is
  that group's membership whatever the format (context/publishing.md).
- Task proof: "A reader in the chosen audience opens the first edition and finds every runbook"
  (context/roadmap/publish.toml).

**Currency**
- cwd: no currency command

**Questions**

1. **What format should the first edition use: a static MkDocs site, a single PDF, or a Markdown
   index page in the repository?**
   - **rec:** a Markdown index page in the repository.
     - The project has no remote and no CI, so a MkDocs site would need a hand build and deploy
       after every edit.
     - A PDF goes stale at the next edit, and old copies stay around.
     - The index page needs no build and never goes stale.
     - One single sign-on group covers every format, so no format reaches more readers.
     - A MkDocs site can be built over the same files later.
   - **changes:** sets the slices:
     - an index page linking all five runbooks,
     - a mkdocs.yml and its build,
     - or a pandoc build of one PDF.
2. **Who is the first edition for: on-call engineers only, or on-call engineers and the support
   team?**
   - **rec:** on-call engineers and support.
     - Support asked for read access in the last quarterly review.
     - The redaction is three lines in three runbooks: two hosts, `db-primary-01.int.example.net`
       and `jobs-01.int.example.net`, and the secret path `secret/platform/acme-token`.
     - Adding support later would need the same pass then.
   - **changes:** including support adds two things:
     - a slice that redacts those three lines, so on-call loses the exact names in the text;
     - a rule that keeps new runbooks clean.
     
     On-call only leaves the runbooks as written and adds no rule.
3. **Where does first-edition end? The repository has no remote and no `[remote] publish`. It can
   end when the edition merges into the local `main`, and you put it behind single sign-on by
   hand. Or this task can first give the project a remote that a session publishes to.**
   - **rec:** end at the local merge.
     - The session brief lists the hand step under Needs you.
     - You check the proof once the edition is in place.
     - A remote and CI become a backlog goal.
   - **changes:**
     - Ending at the local merge keeps the task to the edition's own slices and adds a backlog
       goal for a remote and CI.
     - A remote first puts the remote and `[remote] publish` setup ahead of the edition.

**reply:** "1 ok, 2 ok, 3 ok"

---

Your answers decide what round 2 asks:
- **If support is in the audience:** how to keep new runbooks clean. It could be a denylist in
  `scripts/check.sh`, a STANDARDS.md line, or both.
- **If the format is the index page:** whether the check should fail when a runbook is missing from
  the index. It may also ask whether the check should cover links that don't start with `./`.
